instructions.text_en: Prick the aubergines and char them over a gas flame or barbecue, turning until the skins are blackened and the flesh is soft.
Cover briefly to steam, peel, then leave the flesh in a sieve to drain.
Mash the aubergine coarsely; avoid turning it into a completely smooth purée.
Mix with crushed garlic, tahini, lemon juice and salt. Add yoghurt only if desired.
Spread on a plate and finish with olive oil, pomegranate seeds, parsley and a little red pepper.

instructions.text_en: Peel the potatoes and carefully hollow out the centre of each one, leaving enough potato around the sides to hold its shape.
Prepare the meat filling by cooking the ground lamb and onions with butter, salt and pepper until the meat is cooked and the onions are soft.
Toast the pine nuts separately until lightly golden, then mix them into the meat filling.
Fill each hollowed potato with the prepared mixture.
Arrange the stuffed potatoes in a cooking pot or baking dish.
Pour the tomato juice around the potatoes, adding enough liquid to cook them without washing out the filling.
Cover and cook gently until the potatoes are tender and the filling is thoroughly cooked.
Serve warm with some of the tomato sauce.

instructions.text_en: Rinse the coarse bulgur under cold water and drain thoroughly.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the pearl onions and sauté until softened and lightly golden.
Add the inferred tomatoes, chopped or grated, and cook until softened and their juices are released.
Add the chickpeas and stir gently to combine.
Add the caraway seeds, cinnamon stick, mild white pepper and salt.
Add the drained bulgur and stir until coated with the tomato mixture.
Gradually add water as needed to cook the bulgur. Water is used as a cooking liquid and is not listed as an ingredient in the original reference.
Cover and simmer over low heat until the bulgur is tender and has absorbed most of the liquid.
Remove the cinnamon stick and allow the dish to rest briefly before serving.

instructions.text_en: Combine the flour, salt, yeast and sugar in a mixing bowl.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover it and leave it to rest.
Prepare the filling by heating olive oil in a pan. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add the ground beef, salt, black pepper and cinnamon. Cook until the meat is browned and thoroughly cooked.
Stir in the pine nuts and chopped parsley, then allow the filling to cool.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet and cut it into small circles.
Place a small portion of filling in the centre of each circle. Fold the dough over the filling and seal the edges to form small dumplings.
Arrange the dumplings on a baking tray and bake until lightly golden.
Prepare the yogurt stew by mixing yogurt, water and starch until smooth.
Heat the mixture gently, stirring continuously to prevent the yogurt from separating. Add the crushed garlic if using, and season with salt.
Cook the rice separately, then incorporate it into the yogurt stew.
Add the prepared dumplings and simmer gently until heated through and cooked.
Finish with dried mint and serve warm.

recipes.time_notes: Published page states 50 minutes; chickpea soaking takes an additional 18–24 hours. Frying is included in the method but no separate cook-time figure is published.

instructions.text_en: Soak the dried chickpeas in cold water for 18–24 hours, then drain and dry them thoroughly.
Pulse the chickpeas in a food processor until they resemble coarse crumbs, not a paste.
Add parsley, coriander, spring onions, garlic, cumin, ground coriander and salt; pulse until finely chopped and combined.
Mix in the baking powder and refrigerate the mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the sunflower oil to about 175°C. Shape the mixture into small rounds and press sesame seeds onto the outside.
Fry in batches for 3–4 minutes, turning once, until golden. Drain and serve promptly.

notes: The source explicitly specifies dried chickpeas and says not to use canned chickpeas.
The 18–24-hour soak is additional to the stated 50-minute recipe time.
The source identifies this version as Lebanese coastal falafel and notes its herb-forward parsley and coriander mixture.

instructions.text_en: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm water and allow the mixture to become active.
Combine the flour and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Add the yeast mixture and olive oil gradually. Knead until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Cover the dough and leave it in a warm place until it has risen.
Wash and finely chop the spinach. Sprinkle it with salt and allow it to release excess moisture.
Squeeze the spinach thoroughly to remove the released liquid.
Finely chop the onions and combine them with the spinach, pine nuts, lemon juice, sumac and olive oil.
Mix the filling until the ingredients are evenly distributed.
Divide the dough into small portions and roll each portion into a thin circle.
Place some spinach filling in the centre of each circle.
Fold three sides of the dough towards the centre to form a triangular pastry. Pinch the edges firmly to seal.
Arrange the fatayer on a baking tray.
Bake in a preheated oven until the pastries are golden and cooked through.
Allow them to cool slightly before serving.

instructions.text_en: Cook the chickpeas in water until tender. If already cooked, rinse and warm them gently.
Cut the pita bread into small pieces.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and fry the pita pieces until crisp and golden. Remove and drain excess oil.
Prepare the yogurt sauce by combining yogurt, tahini, crushed garlic and vinegar. Mix until smooth.
Chop the tomatoes and onion finely. Prepare the basil leaves.
Arrange the crispy pita pieces in a serving dish.
Add a layer of warm chickpeas over the bread.
Spoon the yogurt and tahini mixture over the chickpeas.
Add the chopped tomatoes, onion and basil.
Toast the pine nuts in a little oil until golden.
Sprinkle the pine nuts over the dish and season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately while the bread retains some of its crispness.

instructions.text_en: Cut the flatbread into bite-sized pieces, coat with about 3 tablespoons of olive oil and bake at 190°C for 8–10 minutes until crisp.
Chop the tomatoes, cucumbers and pepper; slice the radishes, tear the lettuce and pick the purslane leaves.
Whisk crushed garlic with sumac, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice, salt and the remaining olive oil.
Toss the vegetables and herbs with the dressing.
Add most of the crisp bread just before serving, toss once and finish with the remaining bread and a little sumac.

notes: The source describes purslane, sumac and crisp flatbread as defining elements of this village-style fattoush.
The source lists 100 ml olive oil in total and allocates about 3 tablespoons to the bread; the remainder is used in the dressing.
Salt is listed to taste; no numeric amount is supplied.

instructions.text_en: Rinse the broad beans and soak them in water, preferably overnight.
Drain the beans and place them in a pot with fresh water.
Add the baking soda and cook gently until the beans become very tender. Add water as needed.
Drain excess liquid if necessary, while retaining some cooking liquid.
Mash some of the beans lightly, leaving others whole.
Mix the minced garlic with lemon juice and salt.
Combine the garlic-lemon mixture with the warm beans.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve warm.

instructions.text_en: Trim and thoroughly wash the chicory greens.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and add the chicory.
Boil until the greens become tender.
Drain and rinse with cool water, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Chop the cooked greens into manageable pieces.
Slice the onions and cook them gently in olive oil until soft and golden.
Add the chicory and salt to the onions.
Cook together briefly so the greens absorb the olive oil and onion flavor.
Finish with lemon juice and serve warm or at room temperature.

instructions.text_en: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of water.
Drain, coat with half a teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda and stir for about 3 minutes. Add fresh water and simmer for 1–1.5 hours until very soft; skim foam and loose skins.
Blend lemon juice, garlic and salt. Add tahini, then gradually blend in iced water until pale and creamy.
Add the hot cooked chickpeas and blend for 3–4 minutes until smooth, reserving a few chickpeas for garnish.
Spread on a plate, make a shallow well, drizzle with olive oil and garnish with pepper or sumac, parsley and reserved chickpeas.

instructions.text_en: Finely chop the parsley and one portion of the onions.
Combine the minced lamb with parsley, chopped onion, salt, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into kafta patties or an even layer in a baking dish.
Slice the potatoes and fry them in vegetable oil until lightly golden. Set aside.
Slice the remaining onions and red pepper.
Arrange the kafta in a baking dish and add the fried potatoes, onions, and red pepper.
Combine the tomato juice with olive oil, debs roman, and the listed salt and pepper.
Pour the tomato mixture over the kafta and vegetables.
Add the ripe tomatoes, sliced or chopped.
Bake until the kafta is thoroughly cooked and the potatoes are tender.
Allow the dish to rest briefly before serving.

instructions.text_en: Rinse the bulgur briefly and soak it in water until softened.
Drain thoroughly and squeeze out excess moisture.
Finely chop the onions.
Divide the ground meat into two portions, as indicated by the ingredient description.
Combine one portion of meat with the bulgur, salt, allspice, cumin, and some of the chopped onion.
Knead the mixture until it becomes cohesive.
Cook the remaining meat with the remaining onion until browned and thoroughly cooked.
Season the filling with the listed salt and spices as appropriate, without adding new ingredients.
Spread half of the bulgur-meat mixture in an oiled baking dish.
Distribute the cooked meat filling evenly over it.
Cover with the remaining bulgur-meat mixture and smooth the surface.
Score the top into diamond or square portions.
Bake until the kibbeh is thoroughly cooked and the surface is browned.
Rest briefly before cutting and serving.

Carefully hollow out each courgette, keeping the outer walls intact.
Rinse the rice and drain it well.
Combine the minced lamb with the rice, salt, and black pepper.
Add olive oil to the filling and mix until evenly combined.
Stuff each courgette loosely, leaving room for the rice to expand.
Arrange the stuffed courgettes in a cooking pot.
Add water until the courgettes are mostly covered.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat.
Simmer until the courgettes are tender and the rice and meat filling are fully cooked.
Allow the dish to rest briefly before serving.

Place the lentils in a pot with water and cook until they begin to soften.
Rinse and drain the rice.
Add the rice to the lentils.
Season with salt and continue cooking gently until both the lentils and rice are tender.

Remove thick parsley stems. Wash and dry the parsley completely, then finely chop it with a sharp knife. Finely chop the mint as well.
Dice the tomatoes finely and slice the spring onions into thin rings.

Serve immediately with lettuce or cabbage leaves.
